text.p: Sudanese inflation hit 163 percent in the year to the end of July, from 83 percent in January, according to the central statistics office.

Ali Khidr Kambal, secretary general of the federation of employers, blamed government borrowing from the central bank for the increase, saying money supply had grown to 700 billion pounds this year from 26 billion in 1989, when the present government took power in a military coup.
He was speaking at a seminar on inflation and was quoted in the government newspaper Akhbar al-Yom on Tuesday.

The government of Lieutenant-General Omar Hassan al-Bashir has used this method to finance ambitious projects such as rehabilitating railways, developing petroleum finds and revolutionising higher education, he said.
Izz al-Din Ibrahim, minister of state for finance, told the same seminar that the government's battle against inflation was going nowhere and asked the audience for explanations.
The statistics office said inflation rates at the end of each month this year were: January 83 percent, February 95, March 102, April 117, May 122, June 166 and July 163.
